intent: Revert to the iteration-7 geometry, the best raced design (315.3). Sensor y returns from 0.03 m to 0.05 m, because the 0.03 m lead cut slalom progress from 0.186 to 0.075 and oval finish from 75% to 40%. Track 0.10 m, body 0.10 x 0.12 m, mass 0.5 kg, sensor span x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing and 0.016 m footprint all stay fixed. Expected result: score back near 315, with the oval finish rate at 65% or more and s-bend and slalom progress near their iteration-7 values.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Sensor lead y 0.05 m is better than 0.03 m at mass 0.5 kg, so the iteration-7 score should return. (2) The s-bend and slalom max_error of about 0.062 is not caused by lead, mass or span, so the next lever is turn response through wheel_track or controller-side geometry, not sensing. (3) Sensor_size 0.012 with 0.04 m spacing has a 28 mm gap wider than the 25 mm tape, so it may cause centre-line losses; test it only with a 7-sensor array at about 0.027 m spacing. Please report per-track progress, max_error and steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom, plus the oval finish rate.
rationale: Iteration 8 (sensor y 0.03 m, mass 0.5 kg) scored 209.2, below iteration 7's 315.3 at y 0.05 m. The race shows the shorter lead hurt the robot. Oval finish rate fell from 75% to 40%, and oval progress fell from 0.963 to 0.756. Slalom progress collapsed from 0.186 to 0.075. S-bend progress edged up from 0.140 to 0.1435, and max_error stayed at 0.061, inside the 0.065 m limit. The Integrator's rules say to keep y at 0.03 m only if s-bend and slalom both rise above about 0.18. Slalom fell far below that, so the condition is not met. The rule to return y to 0.05 m when s-bend progress falls below 0.14 is borderline, but the slalom and oval regressions make the lead change clearly negative. I therefore return sensor y to 0.05 m and keep every other field at the iteration-7 values, which is the best raced design so far (315.3). Sensor size 0.012 is not tested now because its conditions were not met, and at 0.04 m spacing its 28 mm gap is wider than the tape. This revert is a return to a validated design, not a new change. Expected result: score near 315, with oval finish rate at or above 75%, and s-bend and slalom progress near 0.14 and 0.19. The s-bend and slalom still end off_track at max_error about 0.062, so the next exploration must come from a different lever, not sensor lead.
